chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Washa, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Hamza, from Saeed ibn Qays al-Hamdani, who said:

I looked one day in the war to a man upon whom were two garments, so I moved my horse and behold it was the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). So I said, 'O Commander of the Faithful, in the likes of this (garment) in this place?' He said, 'Yes, O Saeed ibn Qays! There is not a servant except that he has from Allah a guardian and a protector, with him two angels who protect him from falling from the top of a mountain or falling into a well. So when the Decree descends, they leave him alone and with everything.'
ai.seo_question: What is the role of angels in protecting humans from accidental death according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Abu Hamza al-Thumali from Sa'id ibn Qays al-Hamdani, highlights the Shia theological distinction between general divine protection (hafizah) and specific fatal decree (qada). It illustrates that while angels guard humans from accidental or premature death, they release their hold only when the predetermined time of death arrives, underscoring the balance between divine will and human agency.
